# Critique — Pattern 5 (Mental Health)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Diagnosed Conditions (~10%), Current Treatment & Care History (~10%), Functional Impact (~25%), Coping Resources (~25%), Family History & Childhood (~10%), and self-monitoring/mindfulness fillers (~20%). The last few self-monitoring questions (positions 245–255) felt slightly forced as fillers; without the 255-question limit, more slots would have been dedicated to detailed sub-clinical personality traits and stress-coping mechanisms. Questions regarding past hospitalizations and family history of completed suicide came closest to the scope exclusion line, but were included since they represent historical/familial context rather than active acute risk. Overlaps exist with the Substances and Sleep domains (e.g., alcohol recovery, chronic sleep disturbances) because sleep disruption and self-medication are core components of psychiatric status. The V-flag was systematically applied to questions where a "Yes" answer indicates positive, protective coping behaviors or support networks (e.g., having a crisis plan, regular exercise, therapy attendance) to maintain a downstream convention where a stored bit `1` reflects risk or clinical symptoms. To avoid verbatim copyrighted phrasing, we rewrote standard items from the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 from scratch (such as focusing on general difficulty concentrating or relationships, rather than Pfizer's specific two-week symptom counts). The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your mental health symptoms weekly...") as weekly tracking is highly variable and less clinically informative than functional impairment metrics.
